## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `0` | Success / all checks passed |
| `1` | Command ran but

reported a failure (e.g., server unhealthy, conformance failed) |
| `2` | Invalid arguments or configuration |

## Quick triage

workflow

The fastest path from "I have a server URL" to "I know what's wrong":

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables

"}
# 1. One-shot health check (probe + connect + sweep)
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp

# 2. If oauth
_required: get a token\nmcpjam oauth login --url https://your-server.com/mcp \\\n --protocol-version 2025-11-25 --registration dc

r

# 3. Re-run doctor with the token
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp --oauth-access-token $TOKEN

# 4.
Exercise tools directly\nmcpjam tools list --url https://your-server.com/mcp --access-token $TOKEN\nmcpjam tools call --url https
://your-server.com/mcp --access-token $TOKEN \\\n --tool-name my_tool --tool-args @params.json --quiet --format json\n\n# 5. If t
he server exposes MCP Apps, validate the ui:// surface\nmcpjam apps conformance --url https://your-server.com/mcp --access-token $

TOKEN

# 6. Render one UI-capable tool result in Inspector's App Builder.
# --ui opens Inspector by default in a TTY; add --no-
open if browser automation already opened it.\nmcpjam tools call --url https://your-server.com/mcp --access-token $TOKEN \\\n --t

ool-name my_app_tool --tool-args @params.json --ui --quiet --format json
```

## Use from an MCP client instead of a shell

I
f your agent speaks MCP but can't run shell commands (Claude Desktop, chat clients), run the same testing engine as a stdio MCP se

rver:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
npx -y @mcpjam/cli@latest mcp
```

Connections to servers under test stay
open between tool calls, so agents can also observe notifications and session behavior that one-shot CLI commands can't. See [MCP

Jam as an MCP server](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/mcp-server.md).

# MCP
Jam API\n\n> Programmatic access to the MCP servers in your MCPJam projects — diagnostics, tool calls, prompt rendering, and async

hronous eval runs.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **The MCPJam API is in preview.** It works today and we use it ourselves, but
> it has n
ot been generally announced and the surface may change — including in\n> breaking ways — while we finish the design. Pin your inte
gration to the\n> behaviors documented on this page, build a [tolerant\n> reader](#versioning--stability), and expect to revisit i
t. Feedback is very\n> welcome on [Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) or\n> [GitHub](https://github.com/MCPJam/inspector/issu

es).

> [card] [Create an API key](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)
>
> Go straight to key management in the hosted a

pp. If you're signed out,
> you'll be asked to sign in and then land right back on the API keys page.

The MCPJam API lets you
operate the MCP servers saved in your\n[hosted](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hosted/overview.md) projects — from CI, scripts, or your o

wn agents —
without opening the UI.

What you can do with it today:

* **Discover your resources** — list your projects, thei

r servers, eval
 suites, and chat sessions, so every ID the other routes need is
 self-serve
* **Validate a server** — connec
t, initialize, and capture a capability snapshot\n* **Run the doctor** — the probe → connect → initialize → capabilities workflow\
n* **Check OAuth requirements** — does this server need an OAuth grant?\n* **List tools, prompts, and resources** — the server's M
CP primitives\n* **Call a tool / render a prompt** — execute primitives and get the MCP result back verbatim\n* **Read a resource*
* by URI\n* **Export a full snapshot** — tools, resources, and prompts as one JSON document\n* **Manage a project's clients** — li
st, read, **create** (from a built-in\n template like `claude`/`chatgpt`/`cursor`, or from a full config), edit,\n duplicate, an
d delete the named, reusable configurations that define how\n MCPJam connects to and talks to your MCP servers. Edits are compare
-and-set:\n read the client, then send its `configId` back as `expectedConfigId` for a\n config change and its `name` back as `e
xpectedName` for a rename — a rename\n does not rotate the config, so the config token cannot detect a concurrent\n one — and a
concurrent edit is rejected rather than silently reverted\n* **Manage a project's environments** — list, read, create, edit, archi
ve, and\n restore the named execution bundles (host + optional server group + optional\n pinned skills and plugin versions) that
eval suites and goals run against,\n and **preview** what one resolves to before launching it\n* **List a project's studies** —
name, access mode, attached servers, and\n share link — and **read one study's settings**: model, system prompt,\n tool-approval
policy, and resolved servers\n* **Author eval suites** — create a runnable suite (name, default model, servers, test cases) synch
ronously and get a `suiteId` back; no run is started and no credits are spent\n* **Run eval suites asynchronously** — create a run
from a saved suite, get a `202` + `runId`\n immediately, then poll status, per-iteration results (tool calls, token\n usage, la
tency), and full traces. Runs appear live in the hosted UI,\n tagged `source: \"api\"`\n* **Manage a server's accounts** — comple
te OAuth yourself (e.g. the SDK's\n `runOAuthLogin`, or your CI's own sign-in) and upload the token to a named\n account; list,
rename, choose the default, and delete accounts. Tokens are\n write-only: no route returns one\n* **Run a headless agent turn** —
send a message history, get back the\n assistant reply, the platform operations it invoked, references to any\n resources it cr
eated (eval suites), and token usage; the model is pinned\n server-side and billed to the project\n* **Send feedback** — report a
bug, a missing capability, or something\n confusing to the MCPJam team at the moment you hit it; the same endpoint the\n `send_

feedback` MCP tool calls

All endpoints operate on servers you have already added to a project in the
hosted inspector. Managin

g API keys remains UI-only — see
[Not in the API yet](#not-in-the-api-yet).

## Base URL

```text theme={"theme":"css-vari

ables"}
https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1
```

The API is path-versioned. All routes on this page are relative to the base
URL a

bove.

## Authentication

Every request needs an MCPJam API key in the `Authorization` header:

```bash theme={"theme":"c
ss-variables\"}\ncurl -X POST \\\n \"https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/tools\" \\\n -H \"Aut

horization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{}'
```

### Creating a key

1. Op
en [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)\n in the hosted app (the card at the top of this page tak

es you there
 directly).
2. Click **Create API key**, name it, and pick the **organization** it will act in.
3. Copy the key
